title: Purification and Sequencing of Large Circular DNA from Human Cells
protocol: Cultivate between 1 x 10^6 and 1.0 x 10^7 cells.
Trypsinize cells and centrifuge up to 1.0 x 10^7 cells at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully, avoiding disruption of the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 180 µL of 50 mM TrisHCl and 10 mM EDTA solution.
Transfer the sample to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 µL of proteinase K and mix by tapping the tube.
Place the sample in a thermomixer or shaker-incubator.
Incubate at 56°C while shaking at 900 rpm for 2 hours.
Add 4 µL of RNase A (100 mg/mL) and incubate for 2 minutes at 25°C.
Add 150 µL Buffer AL and mix well by pipetting up and down.
Add 280 µL Buffer MB and vortex for 2 minutes.
Vortex Suspension G before adding to the sample to ensure full resuspension.
Add 40 µL of MagAttract Suspension G to the sample and shake at 1400 rpm for 2 minutes.
Place the sample tube in a magnetic rack and wait approximately 1 minute for bead separation to be complete.
Carefully remove all of the supernatant in the tube and avoid disturbing the magnetic bead pellet.
Add 700 µL of Buffer MW1 and shake at 1400 rpm for 2 minutes.
Place the sample tube on the magnetic rack, wait 1 minute for separation, and remove supernatant while avoiding disruption of the magnetic bead pellet.
Add another 700 µL of Buffer MW1 and shake at 1400 rpm for 2 minutes.
Repeat step by placing sample tube on the magnetic rack, waiting 1 minute for separation, and removing supernatant while avoiding disruption of the magnetic bead pellet.
Add 700 µL of Buffer PM and shake at 1400 rpm for 2 minutes.
Place the sample tube in a magnetic rack and wait approximately 1 minute for bead separation to be complete.
Carefully remove all of the supernatant in the tube and avoid disturbing the magnetic bead pellet.
Carefully add 700 μL of distilled, nuclease-free water to the sample tube while it is on the magnetic rack.
Incubate the tube on the magnetic rack for 1 minute at 25°C.
Remove the supernatant after incubation.
Remove the sample tube from the magnetic rack.
Add 200 μL distilled, nuclease-free water and shake at 1400 rpm for 3 minutes.
Place the sample tube back on the magnetic rack and wait 1 minute for bead separation.
Transfer the supernatant to a new sample tube.
Incubate the MssI reaction at 37°C for 16 hours.
Heat inactivate the endonuclease by incubating at 80°C for 5 minutes.
Treat the reaction with Plasmid-Safe exonuclease to facilitate digestion of linear DNA.
Add 2 µL of Plasmid-Safe ATP-Dependent DNase to the reaction.
Add 4 µL of ATP to the reaction.
Add 10 µL of Plasmid-Safe 10x Reaction Buffer to the reaction.
Add 34 µL of distilled, nuclease-free water to the reaction for a total volume of 100 µL.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 24 hours.
After each 24-hour incubation, add 2 µL of Plasmid-Safe ATP-Dependent DNase to continue enzymatic digestion.
After each 24-hour incubation, add 4 µL of ATP to continue enzymatic digestion.
After each 24-hour incubation, add 0.6 µL of Plasmid-Safe 10x Reaction Buffer to continue enzymatic digestion.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 5 days with daily addition of enzymes and buffer.
Heat inactivate the exonuclease by incubating the sample at 70°C for 30 minutes after 5 days of digestion.
Sample 2 µL of the exonuclease-digested reaction to confirm elimination of linear chromosomal DNA by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR).
Use primers to amplify a chromosomal marker such as the β-globin gene HBB.
Prepare each qPCR reaction as follows: Add 10 µL SYBR Green Master Mix (2x).
Add 1 µL Beta globin forward primer (10 µM) to the reaction mixture.
Add 1 µL Beta globin reverse primer (10 µM) to the reaction mixture.
Add 1.5 µL Sample DNA to the reaction mixture.
Add 6.5 µL distilled, nuclease-free water to complete the reaction volume.
Run reactions using a standard protocol on a real-time PCR machine.
Place 5 μl of the exonuclease-digested sample into a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Add 5 μl Buffer D1 to the sample and vortex to mix, then centrifuge briefly.
Incubate the sample at 25°C for 3 minutes.
Add 10 µL Buffer N1 to the sample and vortex to mix, then centrifuge briefly.
Prepare the REPLI-g DNA Polymerase master mix as follows: Add 29 μl REPLI-g Mini Reaction Buffer and 1 μl REPLI-g Mini DNA Polymerase.
Add the 30 μl master mix to the 20 μl sample for a total reaction volume of 50 µL.
Incubate the reaction at 30°C for 16 hours.
Heat inactivate the reaction at 65°C for 3 minutes.
Measure the quantity of double-stranded DNA obtained from the MDA reaction fluorometrically using a Qubit Fluorometer.
Vortex AMPure XP beads vigorously to resuspend them fully.
Add 86.5 µL of resuspended beads to the sonicated circular DNA sample.
Mix well by pipetting up and down at least 10 times.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the tube and place it on a magnetic rack.
Wait for 5 minutes until the beads fully separate from the supernatant.
Remove and discard the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Add 400 µL of 80% ethanol to the sample while on the rack.
Rotate the microcentrifuge tube in the rack to ensure thorough wash.
Incubate at 25°C for 30 seconds.
Carefully remove and discard all of the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Use a 10 µL pipet tip if necessary to ensure all residual ethanol is removed.
Repeat the wash described in Step 5.
Allow bead pellet to air dry for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add 58 µL of distilled, nuclease-free water to the bead pellet.
Vortex to mix.
Incubate at 25°C for 2 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the tube.
Place the tube on the magnetic rack.
Wait for 5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant containing the DNA to a new tube.
Shear amplified circular DNA with a focused ultrasonicator for an average target peak size of 150 - 200 bp.
Use Peak power: 175.0 W.
Set Duty factor: 10.0.
Set Cycles/burst: 200.
Set Temperature: 6°C.
Shear time: 6 minutes.
Transfer sonicated circular DNA to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

Using the NEBNext Ultra DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina, prepare the end repair reaction for sheared DNA in a 0.2 mL PCR tube as follows: Add 3.0 µL End Prep Enzyme Mix and 6.5 µL End Repair Reaction Buffer (10X) to 55.5 µL sheared DNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down, then briefly centrifuge to remove liquid from the tube sides.
Place the PCR tube in a thermocycler and run an end repair reaction at 20°C for 30 minutes.
Continue with the end repair reaction at 65°C for 30 minutes.
Cool the reaction to 4°C until ready to proceed.
Add 15 µL Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix, 2.5 µL NEBNext Adaptor for Illumina, and 1 µL Ligation enhancer to the end repair reaction.
Mix by pipetting up and down, then briefly centrifuge to remove liquid from the tube sides.
Incubate the tube at 20°C for 15 minutes to carry out the adaptor ligation reaction.
Add 3 µL of USER enzyme to the adaptor ligation reaction and mix well.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Vortex AMPure XP Beads vigorously to ensure they are fully resuspended.
Add 13.5 µL of distilled, nuclease-free water to the adaptor-ligated sample to bring the total volume up to 100 µL.
Add 55 µL of AMPure XP Beads to the sample. Mix by pipetting up and down at least 10 times.
Incubate at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the sample and place it in a magnetic rack. Wait 5 minutes to allow the beads to fully separate from the supernatant.
Transfer the supernatant containing the adaptor-ligated sample to a new microcentrifuge tube. Be careful not to disturb the magnetic bead pellet while removing the supernatant.
Discard the magnetic bead pellet.
Add 25 µL of AMPure XP Beads to the supernatant. Mix thoroughly and incubate at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the sample and place it in a magnetic rack. Wait 5 minutes to allow the beads to fully separate from the supernatant.
Remove and discard the supernatant. Be careful not to disturb the magnetic bead pellet that contains the desired DNA targets.
Add 400 μL of 80% ethanol to the tube while in the magnetic rack.
Rotate the tube to ensure the bead pellet is thoroughly washed.
Incubate at 25°C for 30 seconds and then remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash using a 10 µL pipet tip if necessary to ensure all residual ethanol is removed from the tube.
Open the sample tube on the magnetic rack and allow the magnetic bead pellet to air dry for 5 minutes.
Remove the sample tube from the magnetic rack.
Elute the DNA by adding 17 μL of distilled, nuclease-free water to the magnetic bead pellet.
Mix well by vortexing and then incubate at 25°C for 2 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the tube and then place it on the magnetic rack.
Wait 5 minutes for the beads to fully separate from the supernatant.
Transfer the supernatant containing the size-selected, adaptor-ligated DNA targets to a new tube.
Vortex AMPure XP Beads vigorously to ensure they are fully resuspended.
Add 45 µL of AMPure XP Beads to the sample and mix by pipetting up and down at least 10 times.
Incubate at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the tube and place it on a magnetic rack. Wait for 5 minutes before removing and discarding the supernatant carefully.
Add 400 µL of 80% ethanol to the tube while in the magnetic rack. Rotate the tube to ensure thorough washing of the bead pellet.
Incubate at 25°C for 30 seconds and then remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash using 400 µL of 80% ethanol, ensuring all residual ethanol is removed from the tube.
Open the sample tube on the magnetic rack and allow to airdry the magnetic bead pellet for 5 minutes.
Remove the sample tube from the magnetic rack. Add 33 µL of distilled, nuclease-free water to elute the DNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Centrifuge the tube briefly.
Incubate the tube at 25°C for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge the tube briefly.
Place the tube on the magnetic rack.
Wait 5 minutes for the beads to separate from the supernatant.
Transfer the supernatant containing the size-selected, adaptor-ligated libraries to a new tube.
Store the libraries at -20°C.
Dilute 2-3 µL of the library with distilled, nuclease-free water 5-fold.
Use an Agilent Bioanalyzer high sensitivity chip to verify the size of amplified library fragments.
Remove buffer HT1 from storage at -20°C and allow it to thaw at 25°C.
Store the thawed buffer HT1 at 4°C until ready for use.
Remove the reagent cartridge from storage at -20°C.
Place the cartridge in a 25°C water bath with enough water to submerge up to the line.
Allow the cartridge to thaw in the water bath for approximately 1 hour.
Remove the cartridge from the water bath and gently tap it to remove excess water from the base.
Dry the base of the cartridge thoroughly, ensuring no water has splashed on the top.
Invert the reagent cartridge 10 times to mix the reagents.
Visually inspect position 1 to ensure reagents are fully mixed and no precipitates have formed.
Gently tap the cartridge on the benchtop to remove air bubbles from the reagents.
Store cartridge at 4°C if not proceeding directly to sample run.
Clean the foil seal over the reservoir labeled “Load Samples” with a Kim Wipe.
Pierce the seal above the Load Samples reservoir with a 1000 µL pipette tip.
Pipette up to 600 µL of libraries into the Load Samples reservoir without touching the foil seal.
Select “Manage Instrument” on the Home screen.
Select “Reboot” to reboot the system software.
Select “Sequence” on the Home screen to begin setting up the run.
From the BaseSpace Options screen, select or clear the checkboxes marked “Use BaseSpace for storage and analysis” and “Use BaseSpace Onsite for storage and analysis”.
Select “Next”.
Wear gloves and use plastic forceps to remove the flow cell from its container by gripping it at the base of the plastic cartridge.
Rinse the flow cell with distilled water until all excess salts have been removed from the glass and plastic cartridge.
Clean the flow cell and cartridge with a lint-free lens cleaning tissue.
Pat dry the black flow cell port gasket area and adjacent glass.
Clean the flow cell with an alcohol wipe.
Dry remaining alcohol with a Kim Wipe.
Ensure that the flow cell ports are unobstructed and that the gasket is well-seated around the flow cell ports.
Press the release button on the right of the flow cell latch to open it.
Clean the flow cell stage with ethanol or isopropanol if necessary.
Place the flow cell on the flow cell stage while holding the flow cell by its edges.
Carefully press down on the flow cell latch to close it over the flow cell.
Close the flow cell compartment door and select “Next”.
Remove bottle PR2 from storage at 4°C.
Mix bottle PR2 by inverting it and then remove the lid.
Open the reagent compartment door.
Raise the sipper handle until it locks into place.
Remove the wash bottle and load the PR2 bottle.
Discard contents of wash bottle.
Carefully lower the sipper handle.
Ensure the sippers are lowered into the PR2 bottle and waste bottle.
Select “Next”.
Open the reagent chiller door.
Slide the reagent cartridge into the reagent chiller until the cartridge stops sliding while holding the cartridge by the end with the Illumina label.
Close the reagent chiller door.
Close the reagent compartment door.
Review the experiment name, analysis workflow, read length, and folder locations.
Change any of these parameters if necessary.
Select “Next” when ready.
The system will perform a pre-run check to ensure all components are properly in place before beginning the run.
Select “Start Run” after the check has finished and all components have passed.
